why: law: statement that summarizes a vast number of experimental observations, and describes or predicts some aspect of the natural world

card.q: Explain how you could experimentally determine whether the outside temperature is higher or lower than 0 °C (32 °F) without using a thermometer.
card.a: Place a glass of water outside. It will freeze if the temperature is below 0 °C.

card.q: Identify each of the following statements as being most similar to a hypothesis, a law, or a theory. Explain your reasoning. (a) The pressure of a sample of gas is directly proportional to the temperature of the gas. (b) Matter consists of tiny particles that can combine in specific ratios to form substances with specific properties. (c) At a higher temperature, solids (such as salt or sugar) will dissolve better in water.
card.a: (a) law (states a consistently observed phenomenon, can be used for prediction); (b) theory (a widely accepted explanation of the behavior of matter); (c) hypothesis (a tentative explanation, can be investigated by experimentation)

card.q: Identify each of the underlined items as a part of either the macroscopic domain, the microscopic domain, or the symbolic domain of chemistry. For those in the symbolic domain, indicate whether they are symbols for a macroscopic or a microscopic feature. (a) A certain molecule contains one H atom and one Cl atom. (b) Copper wire has a density of about 8 g/cm³. (c) The bottle contains 15 grams of Ni powder. (d) A sulfur molecule is composed of eight sulfur atoms.
card.a: (a) symbolic, microscopic; (b) macroscopic; (c) symbolic, macroscopic; (d) microscopic

card.q: The amount of heat required to melt 2 lbs of ice is twice the amount of heat required to melt 1 lb of ice. Is this observation a macroscopic or microscopic description of chemical behavior? Explain your answer.
card.a: Macroscopic. The heat required is determined from macroscopic properties.

q: Which term matches this definition? “smallest particle of an element that can enter into a chemical combination”
why: atom: smallest particle of an element that can enter into a chemical combination

q: Which term matches this definition? “pure substance that can be decomposed into two or more elements”
why: compound: pure substance that can be decomposed into two or more elements

q: Which term matches this definition? “substance that is composed of a single type of atom; a substance that cannot be decomposed by a chemical change”
why: element: substance that is composed of a single type of atom; a substance that cannot be decomposed by a chemical change

q: Which term matches this definition? “state in which matter has neither definite volume nor shape”
why: gas: state in which matter has neither definite volume nor shape

card.q: What properties distinguish solids from liquids? Liquids from gases? Solids from gases?
card.a: Liquids can change their shape (flow); solids can’t. Gases can undergo large volume changes as pressure changes; liquids do not. Gases flow and change volume; solids do not.

card.q: How does a homogeneous mixture differ from a pure substance? How are they similar?
card.a: The mixture can have a variety of compositions; a pure substance has a definite composition. Both have the same composition from point to point.

card.q: How do molecules of elements and molecules of compounds differ? In what ways are they similar?
card.a: Molecules of elements contain only one type of atom; molecules of compounds contain two or more types of atoms. They are similar in that both are comprised of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.

card.q: Many of the items you purchase are mixtures of pure compounds. Select three of these commercial products and prepare a list of the ingredients that are pure compounds.
card.a: s will vary. Sample answer: Gatorade contains water, sugar, dextrose, citric acid, salt, sodium chloride, monopotassium phosphate, and sucrose acetate isobutyrate.

card.q: Classify each of the following as an element, a compound, or a mixture: (a) iron (b) oxygen (c) mercury oxide (d) pancake syrup (e) carbon dioxide (f) a substance composed of molecules each of which contains one hydrogen atom and one chlorine atom (g) baking soda (h) baking powder
card.a: (a) element; (b) element; (c) compound; (d) mixture; (e) compound; (f) compound; (g) compound; (h) mixture

card.q: How are the molecules in oxygen gas, the molecules in hydrogen gas, and water molecules similar? How do they differ?
card.a: In each case, a molecule consists of two or more combined atoms. They differ in that the types of atoms change from one substance to the next.

card.q: Prepare a list of the principal chemicals consumed and produced during the operation of an automobile.
card.a: Gasoline (a mixture of compounds), oxygen, and to a lesser extent, nitrogen are consumed. Carbon dioxide and water are the principal products. Carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides are produced in lesser amounts.

card.q: When elemental iron corrodes it combines with oxygen in the air to ultimately form red brown iron(III) oxide called rust. (a) If a shiny iron nail with an initial mass of 23.2 g is weighed after being coated in a layer of rust, would you expect the mass to have increased, decreased, or remained the same? Explain. (b) If the mass of the iron nail increases to 24.1 g, what mass of oxygen combined with the iron?
card.a: (a) Increased as it would have combined with oxygen in the air thus increasing the amount of matter and therefore the mass. (b) 0.9 g

q: Which term matches this definition? “property of a substance that is independent of the amount of the substance”
why: intensive property: property of a substance that is independent of the amount of the substance

why: physical change: change in the state or properties of matter that does not involve a change in its chemical composition

card.q: Classify each of the following changes as physical or chemical: (a) condensation of steam (b) burning of gasoline (c) souring of milk (d) dissolving of sugar in water (e) melting of gold
card.a: (a) physical; (b) chemical; (c) chemical; (d) physical; (e) physical

card.q: Explain the difference between extensive properties and intensive properties.
card.a: The value of an extensive property depends upon the amount of matter being considered, whereas the value of an intensive property is the same regardless of the amount of matter being considered.

card.q: The density (d) of a substance is an intensive property that is defined as the ratio of its mass (m) to its volume (V). density = (mass/volume) d = (m/V) Considering that mass and volume are both extensive properties, explain why their ratio, density, is intensive.
card.a: Being extensive properties, both mass and volume are directly proportional to the amount of substance under study. Dividing one extensive property by another will in effect “cancel” this dependence on amount, yielding a ratio that is independent of amount (an intensive property).

card.q: In the following drawing, the green spheres represent atoms of a certain element. The blue spheres represent atoms of another element. If the spheres of different elements touch, they are part of a single unit of a compound. The following chemical change represented by these spheres may violate one of the ideas of Dalton’s atomic theory. Which one?
card.a: The starting materials consist of one green sphere and two blue spheres. The products consist of two green spheres and two blue spheres. This violates Dalton’s postulate that that atoms are not created during a chemical change, but are merely redistributed.

card.q: Identify the postulate of Dalton’s theory that is violated by the following observations: 59.95% of one sample of titanium dioxide is titanium; 60.10% of a different sample of titanium dioxide is titanium.
card.a: This statement violates Dalton’s fourth postulate: In a given compound, the numbers of atoms of each type (and thus also the percentage) always have the same ratio.

card.q: The existence of isotopes violates one of the original ideas of Dalton’s atomic theory. Which one?
card.a: Dalton originally thought that all atoms of a particular element had identical properties, including mass. Thus, the concept of isotopes, in which an element has different masses, was a violation of the original idea. To account for the existence of isotopes, the second postulate of his atomic theory was modified to state that atoms of the same element must have identical chemical properties.

card.q: How are protons and neutrons similar? How are they different?
card.a: Both are subatomic particles that reside in an atom’s nucleus. Both have approximately the same mass. Protons are positively charged, whereas neutrons are uncharged.

card.q: Repeat using an element that has three naturally occurring isotopes.
card.a: Let us use neon as an example. Since there are three isotopes, there is no way to be sure to accurately predict the abundances to make the total of 20.18 amu average atomic mass. Let us guess that the abundances are 9% Ne-22, 91% Ne-20, and only a trace of Ne-21. The average mass would be 20.18 amu. Checking the nature’s mix of isotopes shows that the abundances are 90.48% Ne-20, 9.25% Ne-22, and 0.27% Ne-21, so our guessed amounts have to be slightly adjusted.

card.q: What is the total mass (amu) of carbon in each of the following molecules? (a) CH₄ (b) CHCl₃ (c) C₁₂H₁₀O₆ (d) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃

Determine the molecular mass of the following compounds: (a) (b) (c) (d)
Write a sentence that describes how to determine the number of moles of a compound in a known mass of the compound using its molecular formula.
card.a: Use the molecular formula to find the molar mass; to obtain the number of moles, divide the mass of compound by the molar mass of the compound expressed in grams.

card.q: Which contains the greatest mass of oxygen: 0.75 mol of ethanol (C₂H₅OH), 0.60 mol of formic acid (HCO₂H), or 1.0 mol of water (H₂O)? Explain why.
card.a: Formic acid. Its formula has twice as many oxygen atoms as the other two compounds (one each). Therefore, 0.60 mol of formic acid would be equivalent to 1.20 mol of a compound containing a single oxygen atom.

card.q: How are the molecular mass and the molar mass of a compound similar and how are they different?
card.a: The two masses have the same numerical value, but the units are different: The molecular mass is the mass of 1 molecule while the molar mass is the mass of 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.

card.q: What does it mean to say an equation is balanced? Why is it important for an equation to be balanced?
card.a: An equation is balanced when the same number of each element is represented on the reactant and product sides. Equations must be balanced to accurately reflect the law of conservation of matter.

card.q: Balance the following equations: (a) PCl₅(s) + H₂O(l) ⟶ POCl₃(l) + HCl(aq) (b) Cu(s) + HNO₃(aq) ⟶ Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + NO(g) (c) H₂(g) + I₂(s) ⟶ HI(s) (d) Fe(s) + O₂(g) ⟶ Fe₂O₃(s) (e) Na(s) + H₂O(l) ⟶ NaOH(aq) + H₂(g) (f) (NH₄)₂Cr₂O₇(s) ⟶ Cr₂O₃(s) + N₂(g) + H₂O(g) (g) P₄(s) + Cl₂(g) ⟶ PCl₃(l) (h) PtCl₄(s) ⟶ Pt(s) + Cl₂(g)
card.a: (a) PCl₅(s) + H₂O(l) ⟶ POCl₃(l) + 2HCl(aq); (b) 3Cu(s) + 8HNO₃(aq) ⟶ 3Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) + 4H₂O(l) + 2NO(g); (c) H₂(g) + I₂(s) ⟶ 2HI(s); (d) 4Fe(s) + 3O₂(g) ⟶ 2Fe₂O₃(s); (e) 2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) ⟶ 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g); (f) (NH₄)₂Cr₂O₇(s) ⟶ Cr₂O₃(s) + N₂(g) + 4H₂O(g); (g) P₄(s) + 6Cl₂(g) ⟶ 4PCl₃(l); (h) PtCl₄(s) ⟶ Pt(s) + 2Cl₂(g)

card.q: From the balanced molecular equations, write the complete ionic and net ionic equations for the following: (a) K₂C₂O₄(aq) + Ba(OH)₂(aq) ⟶ 2KOH(aq) + BaC₂O₄(s) (b) Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂SO₄(aq) ⟶ PbSO₄(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) (c) CaCO₃(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) ⟶ CaSO₄(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l)
card.a: (a); 2K⁺(aq) + C₂O₄²⁻(aq) + Ba²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) ⟶ 2K⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) + BaC₂O₄(s) (complete); Ba²⁺(aq) + C₂O₄²⁻(aq) ⟶ BaC₂O₄(s) (net) (b) Pb²⁺(aq) + 2NO₃⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) ⟶ PbSO₄(s) + 2H⁺(aq) + 2NO₃⁻(aq) (complete); Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) ⟶ PbSO₄(s) (net) (c); CaCO₃(s) + 2H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) ⟶ CaSO₄(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) (complete); CaCO₃(s) + 2H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) ⟶ CaSO₄(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) (net)

q: Which term matches this definition? “vigorous redox reaction producing significant amounts of energy in the form of heat and, sometimes, light”

q: Which term matches this definition? “an equation that shows whether each reactant loses or gains electrons in a reaction.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “of relatively low solubility; dissolving only to a slight extent”
why: insoluble: of relatively low solubility; dissolving only to a slight extent

card.q: Indicate what type, or types, of reaction each of the following represents: (a) Ca(s) + Br₂(l) ⟶ CaBr₂(s) (b) Ca (OH)₂(aq) + 2HBr(aq) ⟶ CaBr₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l) (c) C₆H₁₂(l) + 9O₂(g) ⟶ 6CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(g)
card.a: (a) oxidation-reduction (addition); (b) acid-base (neutralization); (c) oxidation-reduction (combustion)

card.q: Silver can be separated from gold because silver dissolves in nitric acid while gold does not. Is the dissolution of silver in nitric acid an acid-base reaction or an oxidation-reduction reaction? Explain your answer.
card.a: It is an oxidation-reduction reaction because the oxidation state of the silver changes during the reaction.

card.q: Determine the oxidation states of the elements in the compounds listed. None of the oxygen-containing compounds are peroxides or superoxides. (a) H₃PO₄ (b) Al(OH)₃ (c) SeO₂ (d) KNO₂ (e) In₂S₃ (f) P₄O₆

Classify the following as acid-base reactions or oxidation-reduction reactions: (a) Na₂S(aq) + 2HCl(aq) ⟶ 2NaCl(aq) + H₂S(g) (b) 2Na(s) + 2HCl(aq) ⟶ 2NaCl(aq) + H₂(g) (c) Mg(s) + Cl₂(g) ⟶ MgCl₂(s) (d) MgO(s) + 2HCl(aq) ⟶ MgCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) (e) K₃P(s) + 2O₂(g) ⟶ K₃PO₄(s) (f) 3KOH(aq) + H₃PO₄(aq) ⟶ K₃PO₄(aq) + 3H₂O(l)
card.a: (a) acid-base; (b) oxidation-reduction: Na is oxidized, H⁺ is reduced; (c) oxidation-reduction: Mg is oxidized, Cl₂ is reduced; (d) acid-base; (e) oxidation-reduction: P³⁻ is oxidized, O₂ is reduced; (f) acid-base

card.q: Complete and balance the following acid-base equations: (a) HCl gas reacts with solid Ca(OH)₂(s). (b) A solution of Sr(OH)₂ is added to a solution of HNO₃.

card.q: Complete and balance the following oxidation-reduction reactions, which give the highest possible oxidation state for the oxidized atoms. card.a: (a) 2Al(s) + 3F₂(g) ⟶ 2AlF₃(s); (b) 2Al(s) + 3CuBr₂(aq) ⟶ 3Cu(s) + 2AlBr₃(aq); (c) P₄(s) + 5O₂(g) ⟶ P₄O₁₀(s); (d) Ca(s) + 2H₂O(l) ⟶ Ca(OH)₂(aq) + H₂(g)

card.q: Complete and balance the equations for the following acid-base neutralization reactions. If water is used as a solvent, write the reactants and products as aqueous ions. (a) Mg(OH)₂(s) + HClO₄(aq) ⟶ (b) SO₃(g) + H₂O(l) ⟶ (assume an excess of water and that the product dissolves) (c) SrO(s) + H₂SO₄(l) ⟶
card.a: (a) Mg(OH)₂(s) + 2HClO₄(aq) ⟶ Mg²⁺(aq) + 2ClO₄⁻(aq) + 2H₂O(l); (b) SO₃(g) + 2H₂O(l) ⟶ H₃O⁺(aq) + HSO₄⁻(aq), (a solution of H₂SO₄); (c) SrO(s) + H₂SO₄(l) ⟶ SrSO₄(s) + H₂O

card.q: A burning match and a bonfire may have the same temperature, yet you would not sit around a burning match on a fall evening to stay warm. Why not?
card.a: The temperature of 1 gram of burning wood is approximately the same for both a match and a bonfire. This is an intensive property and depends on the material (wood). However, the overall amount of produced heat depends on the amount of material; this is an extensive property. The amount of wood in a bonfire is much greater than that in a match; the total amount of produced heat is also much greater, which is why we can sit around a bonfire to stay warm, but a match would not provide enough heat to keep us from getting cold.

card.q: Explain the difference between heat capacity and specific heat of a substance.
card.a: Heat capacity refers to the heat required to raise the temperature of the mass of the substance 1 degree; specific heat refers to the heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of the substance 1 degree. Thus, heat capacity is an extensive property, and specific heat is an intensive one.

why: ionic bond: strong electrostatic force of attraction between cations and anions in an ionic compound

card.q: Does a cation gain protons to form a positive charge or does it lose electrons?
card.a: The protons in the nucleus do not change during normal chemical reactions. Only the outer electrons move. Positive charges form when electrons are lost.

card.q: Which of the following atoms would be expected to form negative ions in binary ionic compounds and which would be expected to form positive ions: P, I, Mg, Cl, In, Cs, O, Pb, Co?
card.a: P, I, Cl, and O would form anions because they are nonmetals. Mg, In, Cs, Pb, and Co would form cations because they are metals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “bond formed when electrons are shared between atoms”

q: Which term matches this definition? “tendency of an atom to attract electrons in a bond to itself”

q: Which term matches this definition? “covalent bond between atoms of different electronegativities; a covalent bond with a positive end and a negative end”

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, nonpolar covalent bond) covalent bond between atoms of identical electronegativities”
why: pure covalent bond: (also, nonpolar covalent bond) covalent bond between atoms of identical electronegativities

card.q: Why is it incorrect to speak of a molecule of solid NaCl?

card.q: From their positions in the periodic table, arrange the atoms in each of the following series in order of increasing electronegativity: (a) C, F, H, N, O (b) Br, Cl, F, H, I (c) F, H, O, P, S (d) Al, H, Na, O, P (e) Ba, H, N, O, As

card.a: N, O, F, and Cl

q: Which term matches this definition? “molecule that contains an odd number of electrons”

why: Lewis symbol: symbol for an element or monatomic ion that uses a dot to represent each valence electron in the element or ion

q: Which term matches this definition? “two (a pair of) valence electrons that are not used to form a covalent bond”

card.q: Correct the following statement: “The bonds in solid PbCl₂ are ionic; the bond in a HCl molecule is covalent. Thus, all of the valence electrons in PbCl₂ are located on the Cl^– ions, and all of the valence electrons in a HCl molecule are shared between the H and Cl atoms.”
card.a: Two valence electrons per Pb atom are transferred to Cl atoms; the resulting Pb²⁺ ion has a 6s² valence shell configuration. Two of the valence electrons in the HCl molecule are shared, and the other six are located on the Cl atom as lone pairs of electrons.

card.q: The arrangement of atoms in several biologically important molecules is given here. Complete the Lewis structures of these molecules by adding multiple bonds and lone pairs. Do not add any more atoms. (a) the amino acid serine: (b) urea: (c) pyruvic acid: (d) uracil: (e) carbonic acid:
How are single, double, and triple bonds similar? How do they differ?
card.a: Each bond includes a sharing of electrons between atoms. Two electrons are shared in a single bond; four electrons are shared in a double bond; and six electrons are shared in a triple bond.

q: Which term matches this definition? “arrangement of atoms in a molecule or ion”
why: molecular structure: arrangement of atoms in a molecule or ion

q: Which term matches this definition? “situation in which one Lewis structure is insufficient to describe the bonding in a molecule and the average of multiple structures is observed”

q: Which term matches this definition? “two or more Lewis structures that have the same arrangement of atoms but different arrangements of electrons”
why: resonance forms: two or more Lewis structures that have the same arrangement of atoms but different arrangements of electrons

q: Which term matches this definition? “average of the resonance forms shown by the individual Lewis structures”
why: resonance hybrid: average of the resonance forms shown by the individual Lewis structures

card.q: Which compound in each of the following pairs has the larger lattice energy? Note: Ba²⁺ and K⁺ have similar radii; S^(2–) and Cl^– have similar radii. Explain your choices. (a) K₂O or Na₂O (b) K₂S or BaS (c) KCl or BaS (d) BaS or BaCl₂

q: Which term matches this definition? “location in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry in which there is another atom at a 180° angle and the equatorial positions are at a 90° angle”
why: axial position: location in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry in which there is another atom at a 180° angle and the equatorial positions are at a 90° angle

q: Which term matches this definition? “angle between any two covalent bonds that share a common atom”
why: bond angle: angle between any two covalent bonds that share a common atom

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, bond length) distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms”
why: bond distance: (also, bond length) distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms

q: Which term matches this definition? “separation of charge in a bond that depends on the difference in electronegativity and the bond distance represented by partial charges or a vector”
why: bond dipole moment: separation of charge in a bond that depends on the difference in electronegativity and the bond distance represented by partial charges or a vector

q: Which term matches this definition? “property of a molecule that describes the separation of charge determined by the sum of the individual bond moments based on the molecular structure”
why: dipole moment: property of a molecule that describes the separation of charge determined by the sum of the individual bond moments based on the molecular structure

q: Which term matches this definition? “arrangement around a central atom of all regions of electron density (bonds, lone pairs, or unpaired electrons)”
why: electron-pair geometry: arrangement around a central atom of all regions of electron density (bonds, lone pairs, or unpaired electrons)

card.q: Explain why the HOH molecule is bent, whereas the HBeH molecule is linear.
card.a: The placement of the two sets of unpaired electrons in water forces the bonds to assume a tetrahedral arrangement, and the resulting HOH molecule is bent. The HBeH molecule (in which Be has only two electrons to bond with the two electrons from the hydrogens) must have the electron pairs as far from one another as possible and is therefore linear.

card.q: Explain the difference between electron-pair geometry and molecular structure.
card.a: Space must be provided for each pair of electrons whether they are in a bond or are present as lone pairs. Electron-pair geometry considers the placement of all electrons. Molecular structure considers only the bonding-pair geometry.

card.q: Explain how a molecule that contains polar bonds can be nonpolar.
card.a: As long as the polar bonds are compensated (for example. two identical atoms are found directly across the central atom from one another), the molecule can be nonpolar.

card.q: Predict the electron pair geometry and the molecular structure of each of the following molecules or ions: (a) SF₆ (b) PCl₅ (c) BeH₂ (d) CH₃⁺
card.a: (a) Both the electron geometry and the molecular structure are octahedral. (b) Both the electron geometry and the molecular structure are trigonal bipyramid. (c) Both the electron geometry and the molecular structure are linear. (d) Both the electron geometry and the molecular structure are trigonal planar.

card.q: Which of the following molecules and ions contain polar bonds? Which of these molecules and ions have dipole moments? (a) ClF₅ (b) ClO₂⁻ (c) TeCl₄²⁻ (d) PCl₃ (e) SeF₄ (f) PH₂⁻ (g) XeF₂
card.a: All of these molecules and ions contain polar bonds. Only ClF₅, ClO₂⁻, PCl₃, SeF₄, and PH₂⁻ have dipole moments.

card.q: Which of the following molecules have dipole moments? (a) CS₂ (b) SeS₂ (c) CCl₂F₂ (d) PCl₃ (P is the central atom) (e) ClNO (N is the central atom)
card.a: SeS₂, CCl₂F₂, PCl₃, and ClNO all have dipole moments.

q: Which term matches this definition? “coexistence of orbitals from two different atoms sharing the same region of space, leading to the formation of a covalent bond”
why: overlap: coexistence of orbitals from two different atoms sharing the same region of space, leading to the formation of a covalent bond

q: Which term matches this definition? “plane separating different lobes of orbitals, where the probability of finding an electron is zero”
why: node: plane separating different lobes of orbitals, where the probability of finding an electron is zero

q: Which term matches this definition? “covalent bond formed by side-by-side overlap of atomic orbitals; the electron density is found on opposite sides of the internuclear axis”
why: pi bond (π bond): covalent bond formed by side-by-side overlap of atomic orbitals; the electron density is found on opposite sides of the internuclear axis

q: Which term matches this definition? “covalent bond formed by overlap of atomic orbitals along the internuclear axis”
why: sigma bond (σ bond): covalent bond formed by overlap of atomic orbitals along the internuclear axis

q: Which term matches this definition? “description of bonding that involves atomic orbitals overlapping to form σ or π bonds, within which pairs of electrons are shared”
why: valence bond theory: description of bonding that involves atomic orbitals overlapping to form σ or π bonds, within which pairs of electrons are shared

card.q: Explain how σ and π bonds are similar and how they are different.
card.a: Similarities: Both types of bonds result from overlap of atomic orbitals on adjacent atoms and contain a maximum of two electrons. Differences: σ bonds are stronger and result from end-to-end overlap and all single bonds are σ bonds; π bonds between the same two atoms are weaker because they result from side-by-side overlap, and multiple bonds contain one or more π bonds (in addition to a σ bond).

card.q: Explain why bonds occur at specific average bond distances instead of the atoms approaching each other infinitely close.
card.a: The specific average bond distance is the distance with the lowest energy. At distances less than the bond distance, the positive charges on the two nuclei repel each other, and the overall energy increases.

card.q: Use valence bond theory to explain the bonding in O₂. Sketch the overlap of the atomic orbitals involved in the bonds in O₂.
card.a: Bonding: One σ bond and one π bond. The s orbitals are filled and do not overlap. The p orbitals overlap along the axis to form a σ bond and side-by-side to form the π bond.

card.q: A friend tells you N₂ has three π bonds due to overlap of the three p-orbitals on each N atom. Do you agree?
card.a: No, two of the p orbitals (one on each N) will be oriented end-to-end and will form a σ bond.

q: Which term matches this definition? “orbital created by combining atomic orbitals on a central atom”
why: hybrid orbital: orbital created by combining atomic orbitals on a central atom

card.q: Why is the concept of hybridization required in valence bond theory?
card.a: Hybridization is introduced to explain the geometry of bonding orbitals in valence bond theory.

card.q: Explain why a carbon atom cannot form five bonds using sp³d hybrid orbitals.
card.a: There are no d orbitals in the valence shell of carbon.

card.a: trigonal planar, sp²; trigonal pyramidal (one lone pair on A) sp³; T-shaped (two lone pairs on A sp³d, or (three lone pairs on A) sp³d²

card.a: (a) XeF₂ (b) (c) linear (d) sp³d

card.q: Write Lewis structures for NF₃ and PF₅. On the basis of hybrid orbitals, explain the fact that NF₃, PF₃, and PF₅ are stable molecules, but NF₅ does not exist.
card.a: Phosphorus and nitrogen can form sp³ hybrids to form three bonds and hold one lone pair in PF₃ and NF₃, respectively. However, nitrogen has no valence d orbitals, so it cannot form a set of sp³d hybrid orbitals to bind five fluorine atoms in NF₅. Phosphorus has d orbitals and can bind five fluorine atoms with sp³d hybrid orbitals in PF₅.

card.q: The bond energy of a C–C single bond averages 347 kJ mol⁻¹; that of a C≡C triple bond averages 839 kJ mol⁻¹. Explain why the triple bond is not three times as strong as a single bond.
card.a: A triple bond consists of one σ bond and two π bonds. A σ bond is stronger than a π bond due to greater overlap.

card.q: A useful solvent that will dissolve salts as well as organic compounds is the compound acetonitrile, H₃CCN. It is present in paint strippers. (a) Write the Lewis structure for acetonitrile, and indicate the direction of the dipole moment in the molecule. (b) Identify the hybrid orbitals used by the carbon atoms in the molecule to form σ bonds. (c) Describe the atomic orbitals that form the π bonds in the molecule. Note that it is not necessary to hybridize the nitrogen atom.
card.a: (a) (b) The terminal carbon atom uses sp³ hybrid orbitals, while the central carbon atom is sp hybridized. (c) Each of the two π bonds is formed by overlap of a 2p orbital on carbon and a nitrogen 2p orbital.

card.q: Identify the hybridization of the central atom in each of the following molecules and ions that contain multiple bonds: (a) ClNO (N is the central atom) (b) CS₂ (c) Cl₂CO (C is the central atom) (d) Cl₂SO (S is the central atom) (e) SO₂F₂ (S is the central atom) (f) XeO₂F₂ (Xe is the central atom) (g) ClOF₂⁺ (Cl is the central atom)
card.a: (a) sp²; (b) sp; (c) sp²; (d) sp³; (e) sp³; (f) sp³d; (g) sp³

card.q: For each of the following molecules, indicate the hybridization requested and whether or not the electrons will be delocalized: (a) ozone (O₃) central O hybridization (b) carbon dioxide (CO₂) central C hybridization (c) nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) central N hybridization (d) phosphate ion (PO₄³⁻) central P hybridization
card.a: (a) sp², delocalized; (b) sp, localized; (c) sp², delocalized; (d) sp³, delocalized

card.q: Draw the orbital diagram for carbon in CO₂ showing how many carbon atom electrons are in each orbital.
card.a: Each of the four electrons is in a separate orbital and overlaps with an electron on an oxygen atom.

q: Which term matches this definition? “molecular orbital located outside of the region between two nuclei; electrons in an antibonding orbital destabilize the molecule”

q: Which term matches this definition? “number of pairs of electrons between two atoms; it can be found by the number of bonds in a Lewis structure or by the difference between the number of bonding and antibonding electrons divided by two”

q: Which term matches this definition? “molecular orbital located between two nuclei; electrons in a bonding orbital stabilize a molecule”

q: Which term matches this definition? “phenomenon in which a material is not magnetic itself but is repelled by a magnetic field; it occurs when there are only paired electrons present”
why: diamagnetism: phenomenon in which a material is not magnetic itself but is repelled by a magnetic field; it occurs when there are only paired electrons present

q: Which term matches this definition? “molecule consisting of two identical atoms”
why: homonuclear diatomic molecule: molecule consisting of two identical atoms

card.q: How are the following similar, and how do they differ? (a) σ molecular orbitals and π molecular orbitals (b) ψ for an atomic orbital and ψ for a molecular orbital (c) bonding orbitals and antibonding orbitals
card.a: (a) Similarities: Both are bonding orbitals that can contain a maximum of two electrons. Differences: σ orbitals are end-to-end combinations of atomic orbitals, whereas π orbitals are formed by side-by-side overlap of orbitals. (b) Similarities: Both are quantum-mechanical constructs that represent the probability of finding the electron about the atom or the molecule. Differences: ψ for an atomic orbital describes the behavior of only one electron at a time based on the atom. For a molecule, ψ represents a mathematical combination of atomic orbitals. (c) Similarities: Both are orbitals that can contain two electrons. Differences: Bonding orbitals result in holding two or more atoms together. Antibonding orbitals have the effect of destabilizing any bonding that has occurred.

card.q: Can a molecule with an odd number of electrons ever be diamagnetic? Explain why or why not.
card.a: An odd number of electrons can never be paired, regardless of the arrangement of the molecular orbitals. It will always be paramagnetic.

card.q: Why are bonding molecular orbitals lower in energy than the parent atomic orbitals?
card.a: Bonding orbitals have electron density in close proximity to more than one nucleus. The interaction between the bonding positively charged nuclei and negatively charged electrons stabilizes the system.

card.q: Explain why an electron in the bonding molecular orbital in the H₂ molecule has a lower energy than an electron in the 1s atomic orbital of either of the separated hydrogen atoms.
card.a: The pairing of the two bonding electrons lowers the energy of the system relative to the energy of the nonbonded electrons.

card.q: Determine the bond order of each member of the following groups, and determine which member of each group is predicted by the molecular orbital model to have the strongest bond. (a) H₂, H₂⁺, H₂⁻ (b) O₂, O₂²⁺, O₂²⁻ (c) Li₂, Be₂⁺, Be₂ (d) F₂, F₂⁺, F₂⁻ (e) N₂, N₂⁺, N₂⁻
card.a: (a) H₂ bond order = 1, H₂⁺ bond order = 0.5, H₂⁻ bond order = 0.5, strongest bond is H₂; (b) O₂ bond order = 2, O₂²⁺ bond order = 3; O₂²⁻ bond order = 1, strongest bond is O₂²⁺; (c) Li₂ bond order = 1, Be₂⁺ bond order = 0.5, Be₂ bond order = 0, strongest bond is Li₂;(d) F₂ bond order = 1, F₂⁺ bond order = 1.5, F₂⁻ bond order = 0.5, strongest bond is F₂⁺; (e) N₂ bond order = 3, N₂⁺ bond order = 2.5, N₂⁻ bond order = 2.5, strongest bond is N₂

card.q: Compare the atomic and molecular orbital diagrams to identify the member of each of the following pairs that has the highest first ionization energy (the most tightly bound electron) in the gas phase: (a) H and H₂ (b) N and N₂ (c) O and O₂ (d) C and C₂ (e) B and B₂
card.a: (a) H₂; (b) N₂; (c) O; (d) C₂; (e) B₂

card.q: A friend tells you that the 2s orbital for fluorine starts off at a much lower energy than the 2s orbital for lithium, so the resulting σ_(2s) molecular orbital in F₂ is more stable than in Li₂. Do you agree?
card.a: Yes, fluorine is a smaller atom than Li, so atoms in the 2s orbital are closer to the nucleus and more stable.

card.q: Explain why N₂²⁺ is diamagnetic, while O₂⁴⁺, which has the same number of valence electrons, is paramagnetic.
card.a: N₂ has s-p mixing, so the π orbitals are the last filled in N₂²⁺. O₂ does not have s-p mixing, so the σ_p orbital fills before the π orbitals.

card.q: Why are sharp knives more effective than dull knives? (Hint: Think about the definition of pressure.)
card.a: The cutting edge of a knife that has been sharpened has a smaller surface area than a dull knife. Since pressure is force per unit area, a sharp knife will exert a higher pressure with the same amount of force and cut through material more effectively.

card.q: Why should you roll or belly-crawl rather than walk across a thinly-frozen pond?
card.a: Lying down distributes your weight over a larger surface area, exerting less pressure on the ice compared to standing up. If you exert less pressure, you are less likely to break through thin ice.

card.a: 4.2 hours

card.q: Starting with the definition of rate of effusion and Graham’s finding relating rate and molar mass, show how to derive the Graham’s law equation, relating the relative rates of effusion for two gases to their molecular masses.
card.a: Effusion can be defined as the process by which a gas escapes through a pinhole into a vacuum. Graham’s law states that with a mixture of two gases A and B: ((rate A)/(rate B)) = ((molar mass of B)/(molar mass of A))^(1/2). Both A and B are in the same container at the same temperature, and therefore will have the same kinetic energy: KE_A = KE_BKE = (1/2) mv² Therefore, (1/2)m_Av_A² = (1/2)m_Bv_B² ((v_A²)/(v_B²)) = (m_B/m_A) ((v_A²)/(v_B²))^(1/2) = (m_B/m_A)^(1/2) (v_A/v_B) = (m_B/m_A)^(1/2)

card.q: Which of the following gases diffuse more slowly than oxygen? F₂, Ne, N₂O, C₂H₂, NO, Cl₂, H₂S
card.a: F₂, N₂O, Cl₂, H₂S

q: Which term matches this definition? “theory based on simple principles and assumptions that effectively explains ideal gas behavior”

q: Which term matches this definition? “measure of average speed for a group of particles calculated as the square root of the average squared speed”

card.q: Can the speed of a given molecule in a gas double at constant temperature? Explain your answer.
card.a: Yes. At any given instant, there are a range of values of molecular speeds in a sample of gas. Any single molecule can speed up or slow down as it collides with other molecules. The average speed of all the molecules is constant at constant temperature.

card.q: The distribution of molecular speeds in a sample of helium is shown in. If the sample is cooled, will the distribution of speeds look more like that of H₂ or of H₂O? Explain your answer.
card.a: H₂O. Cooling slows the speeds of the He atoms, causing them to behave as though they were heavier.

card.q: A 1-L sample of CO initially at STP is heated to 546 K, and its volume is increased to 2 L.(a) What effect do these changes have on the pressure exerted by the gas? (b) What is the effect on the average kinetic energy of the molecules? (c) What is the effect on the root mean square speed of the molecules?
card.a: (a) The pressure of the gas remains constant. (b) The average kinetic energy doubles. (c) The root mean square speed increases to √2 times its initial value; u_(rms) is proportional to √(KE_(avg)).

q: Which term matches this definition? “ratio of the experimentally measured molar volume for a gas to its molar volume as computed from the ideal gas equation”
why: compressibility factor (Z): ratio of the experimentally measured molar volume for a gas to its molar volume as computed from the ideal gas equation

q: Which term matches this definition? “modified version of the ideal gas equation containing additional terms to account for non-ideal gas behavior”

card.q: Graphs showing the behavior of several different gases follow. Which of these gases exhibit behavior significantly different from that expected for ideal gases?
card.a: Gases C, E, and F

card.q: Under which of the following sets of conditions does a real gas behave most like an ideal gas, and for which conditions is a real gas expected to deviate from ideal behavior? Explain. (a) high pressure, small volume (b) high temperature, low pressure (c) low temperature, high pressure
card.a: The gas behavior most like an ideal gas will occur under the conditions that minimize the chances of significant interactions between the gaseous atoms/molecules, namely, low pressures (fewer atoms/molecules per unit volume) and high temperatures (greater kinetic energies of atoms/molecules make them less susceptible to attractive forces). The conditions described in (b), high temperature and low pressure, are therefore most likely to yield ideal gas behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “intermolecular attraction between two permanent dipoles”

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, London dispersion force) attraction between two rapidly fluctuating, temporary dipoles; significant only when particles are very close together”

q: Which term matches this definition? “occurs when exceptionally strong dipoles attract; bonding that exists when hydrogen is bonded to one of the three most electronegative elements: F, O, or N”
why: hydrogen bonding: occurs when exceptionally strong dipoles attract; bonding that exists when hydrogen is bonded to one of the three most electronegative elements: F, O, or N

q: Which term matches this definition? “temporary dipole formed when the electrons of an atom or molecule are distorted by the instantaneous dipole of a neighboring atom or molecule”
why: induced dipole: temporary dipole formed when the electrons of an atom or molecule are distorted by the instantaneous dipole of a neighboring atom or molecule

q: Which term matches this definition? “temporary dipole that occurs for a brief moment in time when the electrons of an atom or molecule are distributed asymmetrically”

q: Which term matches this definition? “noncovalent attractive force between atoms, molecules, and/or ions”
why: intermolecular force: noncovalent attractive force between atoms, molecules, and/or ions

card.q: In terms of their bulk properties, how do liquids and solids differ? How are they similar?
card.a: Liquids and solids are similar in that they are matter composed of atoms, ions, or molecules. They are incompressible and have similar densities that are both much larger than those of gases. They are different in that liquids have no fixed shape, and solids are rigid.

card.q: In terms of the kinetic molecular theory, in what ways are liquids similar to gases? In what ways are liquids different from gases?
card.a: They are similar in that the atoms or molecules are free to move from one position to another. They differ in that the particles of a liquid are confined to the shape of the vessel in which they are placed. In contrast, a gas will expand without limit to fill the space into which it is placed.

card.q: What is the evidence that all neutral atoms and molecules exert attractive forces on each other?
card.a: All atoms and molecules will condense into a liquid or solid in which the attractive forces exceed the kinetic energy of the molecules, at sufficiently low temperature.

card.q: Why do the boiling points of the noble gases increase in the order He < Ne < Ar < Kr < Xe?
card.a: The London forces typically increase as the number of electrons increase.

card.q: Arrange each of the following sets of compounds in order of increasing boiling point temperature: (a) HCl, H₂O, SiH₄ (b) F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ (c) CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ (d) O₂, NO, N₂
card.a: (a) SiH₄ < HCl < H₂O; (b) F₂ < Cl₂ < Br₂; (c) CH₄ < C₂H₆ < C₃H₈; (d) N₂ < O₂ < NO

card.q: On the basis of intermolecular attractions, explain the differences in the boiling points of n–butane (−1 °C) and chloroethane (12 °C), which have similar molar masses.
card.a: Only rather small dipole-dipole interactions from C-H bonds are available to hold n-butane in the liquid state. Chloroethane, however, has rather large dipole interactions because of the Cl-C bond; the interaction, therefore, is stronger, leading to a higher boiling point.

card.q: The melting point of H₂O(s) is 0 °C. Would you expect the melting point of H₂S(s) to be −85 °C, 0 °C, or 185 °C? Explain your answer.
card.a: −85 °C. Water has stronger hydrogen bonds, so it melts at a higher temperature.

card.q: Explain why a hydrogen bond between two water molecules is weaker than a hydrogen bond between two hydrogen fluoride molecules.
card.a: The hydrogen bond between two hydrogen fluoride molecules is stronger than that between two water molecules because the electronegativity of F is greater than that of O. Consequently, the partial negative charge on F is greater than that on O. The hydrogen bond between the partially positive H and the larger partially negative F will be stronger than that formed between H and O.

q: Which term matches this definition? “force of attraction between molecules of different chemical identities”
why: adhesive force: force of attraction between molecules of different chemical identities

q: Which term matches this definition? “flow of liquid within a porous material due to the attraction of the liquid molecules to the surface of the material and to other liquid molecules”
why: capillary action: flow of liquid within a porous material due to the attraction of the liquid molecules to the surface of the material and to other liquid molecules

q: Which term matches this definition? “force of attraction between identical molecules”
why: cohesive force: force of attraction between identical molecules

q: Which term matches this definition? “energy required to increase the area, or length, of a liquid surface by a given amount”
why: surface tension: energy required to increase the area, or length, of a liquid surface by a given amount

q: Which term matches this definition? “measure of a liquid’s resistance to flow”
why: viscosity: measure of a liquid’s resistance to flow

card.q: Although steel is denser than water, a steel needle or paper clip placed carefully lengthwise on the surface of still water can be made to float. Explain at a molecular level how this is possible.
card.a: The water molecules have strong intermolecular forces of hydrogen bonding. The water molecules are thus attracted strongly to one another and exhibit a relatively large surface tension, forming a type of “skin” at its surface. This skin can support a bug or paper clip if gently placed on the water.

card.q: You may have heard someone use the figure of speech “slower than molasses in winter” to describe a process that occurs slowly. Explain why this is an apt idiom, using concepts of molecular size and shape, molecular interactions, and the effect of changing temperature.
card.a: Temperature has an effect on intermolecular forces: The higher the temperature, the greater the kinetic energies of the molecules and the greater the extent to which their intermolecular forces are overcome, and so the more fluid (less viscous) the liquid. The lower the temperature, the less the intermolecular forces are overcome, and so the less viscous the liquid.

card.q: Water rises in a glass capillary tube to a height of 17 cm. What is the diameter of the capillary tube?

q: Which term matches this definition? “temperature at which the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the pressure of the gas above it”
why: boiling point: temperature at which the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the pressure of the gas above it

q: Which term matches this definition? “mathematical relationship between the temperature, vapor pressure, and enthalpy of vaporization for a substance”
why: Clausius-Clapeyron equation: mathematical relationship between the temperature, vapor pressure, and enthalpy of vaporization for a substance

q: Which term matches this definition? “change from a gaseous to a liquid state”
why: condensation: change from a gaseous to a liquid state

q: Which term matches this definition? “change from a gaseous state directly to a solid state”
why: deposition: change from a gaseous state directly to a solid state

q: Which term matches this definition? “state of a system in which reciprocal processes are occurring at equal rates”
why: dynamic equilibrium: state of a system in which reciprocal processes are occurring at equal rates

q: Which term matches this definition? “change from a liquid state to a solid state”
why: freezing: change from a liquid state to a solid state

card.q: Heat is added to ice at 0 °C. Explain why the temperature of the ice does not change. What does change?
card.a: The heat is absorbed by the ice, providing the energy required to partially overcome intermolecular attractive forces in the solid and causing a phase transition to liquid water. The solution remains at 0 °C until all the ice is melted. Only the amount of water existing as ice changes until the ice disappears. Then the temperature of the water can rise.

card.q: Identify two common observations indicating some liquids have sufficient vapor pressures to noticeably evaporate?
card.a: We can see the amount of liquid in an open container decrease and we can smell the vapor of some liquids.

card.q: What is the relationship between the intermolecular forces in a liquid and its vapor pressure?
card.a: The vapor pressure of a liquid decreases as the strength of its intermolecular forces increases.

card.q: Why does spilled gasoline evaporate more rapidly on a hot day than on a cold day?
card.a: As the temperature increases, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of gasoline increases and so a greater fraction of molecules have sufficient energy to escape from the liquid than at lower temperatures.

card.q: When is the boiling point of a liquid equal to its normal boiling point?
card.a: They are equal when the pressure of gas above the liquid is exactly 1 atm.

card.q: Use the information in to estimate the boiling point of water in Denver when the atmospheric pressure is 83.3 kPa.
card.a: approximately 95 °C

card.q: Explain the following observations: (a) It takes longer to cook an egg in Ft. Davis, Texas (altitude, 5000 feet above sea level) than it does in Boston (at sea level). (b) Perspiring is a mechanism for cooling the body.
card.a: (a) At 5000 feet, the atmospheric pressure is lower than at sea level, and water will therefore boil at a lower temperature. This lower temperature will cause the physical and chemical changes involved in cooking the egg to proceed more slowly, and a longer time is required to fully cook the egg. (b) As long as the air surrounding the body contains less water vapor than the maximum that air can hold at that temperature, perspiration will evaporate, thereby cooling the body by removing the heat of vaporization required to vaporize the water.

card.q: Explain why the molar enthalpies of vaporization of the following substances increase in the order CH₄ < C₂H₆ < C₃H₈, even though the type of IMF (dispersion) is the same.
card.a: Dispersion forces increase with molecular mass or size. As the number of atoms composing the molecules in this homologous series increases, so does the extent of intermolecular attraction via dispersion forces and, consequently, the energy required to overcome these forces and vaporize the liquids.

q: Which term matches this definition? “temperature and pressure above which a gas cannot be condensed into a liquid”
why: critical point: temperature and pressure above which a gas cannot be condensed into a liquid

q: Which term matches this definition? “pressure-temperature graph summarizing conditions under which the phases of a substance can exist”
why: phase diagram: pressure-temperature graph summarizing conditions under which the phases of a substance can exist

q: Which term matches this definition? “substance at a temperature and pressure higher than its critical point; exhibits properties intermediate between those of gaseous and liquid states”
why: supercritical fluid: substance at a temperature and pressure higher than its critical point; exhibits properties intermediate between those of gaseous and liquid states

q: Which term matches this definition? “temperature and pressure at which three phases of a substance are in equilibrium”
why: triple point: temperature and pressure at which three phases of a substance are in equilibrium

card.q: What phase changes will take place when water is subjected to varying pressure at a constant temperature of 0.005 °C? At 40 °C? At −40 °C?
card.a: At low pressures and 0.005 °C, the water is a gas. As the pressure increases to 4.6 torr, the water becomes a solid; as the pressure increases still more, it becomes a liquid. At 40 °C, water at low pressure is a vapor; at pressures higher than about 75 torr, it converts into a liquid. At −40 °C, water goes from a gas to a solid as the pressure increases above very low values.

card.q: From the phase diagram for carbon dioxide in, determine the state of CO₂ at: (a) 20 °C and 1000 kPa (b) 10 °C and 2000 kPa (c) 10 °C and 100 kPa (d) −40 °C and 500 kPa (e) −80 °C and 1500 kPa (f) −80 °C and 10 kPa
card.a: (a) gas; (b) gas; (c) gas; (d) gas; (e) solid; (f) gas

card.q: If a severe storm results in the loss of electricity, it may be necessary to use a clothesline to dry laundry. In many parts of the country in the dead of winter, the clothes will quickly freeze when they are hung on the line. If it does not snow, will they dry anyway? Explain your answer.
card.a: Yes, ice will sublime, although it may take it several days. Ice has a small vapor pressure, and some ice molecules form gas and escape from the ice crystals. As time passes, more and more solid converts to gas until eventually the clothes are dry.

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, noncrystalline solid) solid in which the particles lack an ordered internal structure”
why: amorphous solid: (also, noncrystalline solid) solid in which the particles lack an ordered internal structure

q: Which term matches this definition? “solid whose particles are held together by covalent bonds”
why: covalent network solid: solid whose particles are held together by covalent bonds

q: Which term matches this definition? “solid in which the particles are arranged in a definite repeating pattern”

q: Which term matches this definition? “spaces between the regular particle positions in any array of atoms or ions”
why: interstitial sites: spaces between the regular particle positions in any array of atoms or ions

q: Which term matches this definition? “solid composed of positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic attractions”
why: ionic solid: solid composed of positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic attractions

q: Which term matches this definition? “solid composed of metal atoms”
why: metallic solid: solid composed of metal atoms

card.q: At very low temperatures oxygen, O₂, freezes and forms a crystalline solid. Which best describes these crystals? (a) ionic (b) covalent network (c) metallic (d) amorphous (e) molecular crystals
card.a: (e) molecular crystals

card.q: Explain why ice, which is a crystalline solid, has a melting temperature of 0 °C, whereas butter, which is an amorphous solid, softens over a range of temperatures.
card.a: Ice has a crystalline structure stabilized by hydrogen bonding. These intermolecular forces are of comparable strength and thus require the same amount of energy to overcome. As a result, ice melts at a single temperature and not over a range of temperatures. The various, very large molecules that compose butter experience varied van der Waals attractions of various strengths that are overcome at various temperatures, and so the melting process occurs over a wide temperature range.

card.q: Identify the type of crystalline solid (metallic, network covalent, ionic, or molecular) formed by each of the following substances: (a) CaCl₂ (b) SiC (c) N₂ (d) Fe (e) C (graphite) (f) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (g) HCl (h) NH₄NO₃ (i) K₃PO₄
card.a: (a) ionic; (b) covalent network; (c) molecular; (d) metallic; (e) covalent network; (f) molecular; (g) molecular; (h) ionic; (i) ionic

card.a: X = ionic; Y = metallic; Z = covalent network

card.a: (b) metallic solid

q: Which term matches this definition? “crystalline structure that has a cubic unit cell with lattice points at the corners and in the center of the cell”
why: body-centered cubic (BCC) solid: crystalline structure that has a cubic unit cell with lattice points at the corners and in the center of the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “equation that relates the angles at which X-rays are diffracted by the atoms within a crystal”
why: Bragg equation: equation that relates the angles at which X-rays are diffracted by the atoms within a crystal

q: Which term matches this definition? “number of atoms closest to any given atom in a crystal or to the central metal atom in a complex”

why: cubic closest packing (CCP): crystalline structure in which planes of closely packed atoms or ions are stacked as a series of three alternating layers of different relative orientations (ABC)

why: diffraction: redirection of electromagnetic radiation that occurs when it encounters a physical barrier of appropriate dimensions

card.q: Describe the crystal structure of iron, which crystallizes with two equivalent metal atoms in a cubic unit cell.
card.a: The structure of this low-temperature form of iron (below 910 °C) is body-centered cubic. There is one-eighth atom at each of the eight corners of the cube and one atom in the center of the cube.

card.q: Tungsten crystallizes in a body-centered cubic unit cell with an edge length of 3.165 Å. (a) What is the atomic radius of tungsten in this structure? (b) Calculate the density of tungsten.
Barium crystallizes in a body-centered cubic unit cell with an edge length of 5.025 Å (a) What is the atomic radius of barium in this structure? (b) Calculate the density of barium.
The density of aluminum is 2.7 g/cm³; that of silicon is 2.3 g/cm³. Explain why Si has the lower density even though it has heavier atoms.
card.a: The crystal structure of Si shows that it is less tightly packed (coordination number 4) in the solid than Al (coordination number 12).

card.q: Cadmium sulfide, sometimes used as a yellow pigment by artists, crystallizes with cadmium, occupying one-half of the tetrahedral holes in a closest packed array of sulfide ions. What is the formula of cadmium sulfide? Explain your answer.
card.a: In a closest-packed array, two tetrahedral holes exist for each anion. If only half the tetrahedral holes are occupied, the numbers of anions and cations are equal. The formula for cadmium sulfide is CdS.

card.q: A compound of thallium and iodine crystallizes in a simple cubic array of iodide ions with thallium ions in all of the cubic holes. What is the formula of this iodide? Explain your answer.
card.a: In a simple cubic array, only one cubic hole can be occupied be a cation for each anion in the array. The ratio of thallium to iodide must be 1:1; therefore, the formula for thallium is TlI.

card.q: What is the percent by mass of titanium in rutile, a mineral that contains titanium and oxygen, if structure can be described as a closest packed array of oxide ions with titanium ions in one-half of the octahedral holes? What is the oxidation number of titanium?
card.a: 59.95%; The oxidation number of titanium is +4.

card.q: As minerals were formed from the molten magma, different ions occupied the same cites in the crystals. Lithium often occurs along with magnesium in minerals despite the difference in the charge on their ions. Suggest an explanation.
card.a: Both ions are close in size: Mg, 0.65; Li, 0.60. This similarity allows the two to interchange rather easily. The difference in charge is generally compensated by the switch of Si⁴⁺ for Al³⁺.

q: Which term matches this definition? “solid mixture of a metallic element and one or more additional elements”
why: alloy: solid mixture of a metallic element and one or more additional elements

q: Which term matches this definition? “solution that forms with no accompanying energy change”
why: ideal solution: solution that forms with no accompanying energy change

q: Which term matches this definition? “exothermic process in which intermolecular attractive forces between the solute and solvent in a solution are established”
why: solvation: exothermic process in which intermolecular attractive forces between the solute and solvent in a solution are established

q: Which term matches this definition? “physical or chemical change that occurs without the addition of energy from an external source”
why: spontaneous process: physical or chemical change that occurs without the addition of energy from an external source

card.q: How do solutions differ from compounds? From other mixtures?
card.a: A solution can vary in composition, while a compound cannot vary in composition. Solutions are homogeneous at the molecular level, while other mixtures are heterogeneous.

card.q: When KNO₃ is dissolved in water, the resulting solution is significantly colder than the water was originally. (a) Is the dissolution of KNO₃ an endothermic or an exothermic process? (b) What conclusions can you draw about the intermolecular attractions involved in the process? (c) Is the resulting solution an ideal solution?
card.a: (a) The process is endothermic as the solution is consuming heat. (b) Attraction between the K⁺ and NO₃⁻ ions is stronger than between the ions and water molecules (the ion-ion interactions have a lower, more negative energy). Therefore, the dissolution process increases the energy of the molecular interactions, and it consumes the thermal energy of the solution to make up for the difference. (c) No, an ideal solution is formed with no appreciable heat release or consumption.

card.q: Indicate the most important types of intermolecular attractions in each of the following solutions: (a) The solution in. (b) NO(l) in CO(l) (c) Cl₂(g) in Br₂(l) (d) HCl(g) in benzene C₆H₆(l)(e) Methanol CH₃OH(l) in H₂O(l)
card.a: (a) ion-dipole forces; (b) dipole-dipole forces; (c) dispersion forces; (d) dispersion forces; (e) hydrogen bonding

card.q: Heat is released when some solutions form; heat is absorbed when other solutions form. Provide a molecular explanation for the difference between these two types of spontaneous processes.
card.a: Heat is released when the total intermolecular forces (IMFs) between the solute and solvent molecules are stronger than the total IMFs in the pure solute and in the pure solvent: Breaking weaker IMFs and forming stronger IMFs releases heat. Heat is absorbed when the total IMFs in the solution are weaker than the total of those in the pure solute and in the pure solvent: Breaking stronger IMFs and forming weaker IMFs absorbs heat.

q: Which term matches this definition? “physical process accompanying the dissolution of an ionic compound in which the compound’s constituent ions are solvated and dispersed throughout the solution”
why: dissociation: physical process accompanying the dissolution of an ionic compound in which the compound’s constituent ions are solvated and dispersed throughout the solution

q: Which term matches this definition? “substance that does not produce ions when dissolved in water”

q: Which term matches this definition? “substance that dissociates or ionizes completely when dissolved in water”

q: Which term matches this definition? “substance that ionizes only partially when dissolved in water”

card.q: Explain why the ions Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are strongly solvated in water but not in hexane, a solvent composed of nonpolar molecules.
card.a: Crystals of NaCl dissolve in water, a polar liquid with a very large dipole moment, and the individual ions become strongly solvated. Hexane is a nonpolar liquid with a dipole moment of zero and, therefore, does not significantly interact with the ions of the NaCl crystals.

card.q: Consider the solutions presented: (a) Which of the following sketches best represents the ions in a solution of Fe(NO₃)₃(aq)? (b) Write a balanced chemical equation showing the products of the dissolution of Fe(NO₃)₃.
card.a: (a) Fe(NO₃)₃ is a strong electrolyte, thus it should completely dissociate into Fe³⁺ and NO₃⁻ ions. Therefore, (z) best represents the solution. (b) Fe(NO₃)₃(s) ⟶ Fe³⁺(aq) + 3NO₃⁻(aq)

card.q: What is the expected electrical conductivity of the following solutions? (a) NaOH(aq) (b) HCl(aq) (c) C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) (glucose) (d) NH₃(aq)
card.a: (a) high conductivity (solute is an ionic compound that will dissociate when dissolved); (b) high conductivity (solute is a strong acid and will ionize completely when dissolved); (c) nonconductive (solute is a covalent compound, neither acid nor base, unreactive towards water); (d) low conductivity (solute is a weak base and will partially ionize when dissolved)

card.q: Indicate the most important type of intermolecular attraction responsible for solvation in each of the following solutions: (a) the solutions in (b) methanol, CH₃OH, dissolved in ethanol, C₂H₅OH (c) methane, CH₄, dissolved in benzene, C₆H₆ (d) the polar halocarbon CF₂Cl₂ dissolved in the polar halocarbon CF₂ClCFCl₂ (e) O₂(l) in N₂(l)
card.a: (a) ion-dipole; (b) hydrogen bonds; (c) dispersion forces; (d) dipole-dipole attractions; (e) dispersion forces

q: Which term matches this definition? “the proportional relationship between the concentration of dissolved gas in a solution and the partial pressure of the gas in contact with the solution”
why: Henry’s law: the proportional relationship between the concentration of dissolved gas in a solution and the partial pressure of the gas in contact with the solution

q: Which term matches this definition? “of negligible mutual solubility; typically refers to liquid substances”
why: immiscible: of negligible mutual solubility; typically refers to liquid substances

card.q: Supersaturated solutions of most solids in water are prepared by cooling saturated solutions. Supersaturated solutions of most gases in water are prepared by heating saturated solutions. Explain the reasons for the difference in the two procedures.
card.a: The solubility of solids usually decreases upon cooling a solution, while the solubility of gases usually decreases upon heating.

card.q: What is the microscopic explanation for the macroscopic behavior illustrated in?
card.a: The strength of the bonds between like molecules is stronger than the strength between unlike molecules. Therefore, some regions will exist in which the water molecules will exclude oil molecules and other regions will exist in which oil molecules will exclude water molecules, forming a heterogeneous region.

card.q: A solution of potassium nitrate, an electrolyte, and a solution of glycerin (C₃H₅(OH)₃), a nonelectrolyte, both boil at 100.3 °C. What other physical properties of the two solutions are identical?
card.a: Both form homogeneous solutions; their boiling point elevations are the same, as are their lowering of vapor pressures. Osmotic pressure and the lowering of the freezing point are also the same for both solutions.

why: amphiphilic: molecules possessing both hydrophobic (nonpolar) and a hydrophilic (polar) parts
